checkpoints.description: [1/2] Lift the three-digit IDEA-NNN ceiling so the register can grow past 999

impact_assessment.why: The idea register is full at IDEA-999 with no gaps, and four regexes accept exactly three digits, so the active review's 1000-1004 reservations cannot be written and the new portfolio ideas cannot be registered.
impact_assessment.benefits: Dossier headings, MATRIX rows, commit references and registry validation accept three or more digit ids; existing ids stay valid; the 1000-1004 reservations become usable and the register can grow.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: IDEA parsing widens from exactly 3 to 3+ digits; dependency: none; concurrency: the registry lock is unchanged; state: existing 1-999 rows are untouched and 1000-1004 stay reserved to their review
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for four-digit commit parsing, dossier headings, matrix rows and id validation; full kit suite; idea-catcher validate and render --check

[1/3] Fence reforge review packets as untrusted repository data with a random-id block and an explicit instruction/data boundary

impact_assessment.why: IDEA-909 is approved: reforge packets embed commit subjects and raw hunks from any audited repository, so a hostile commit can address the reviewing agent as if it were the operator
impact_assessment.benefits: The reviewer sees one unambiguous data block; a commit cannot close the random-id fence or smuggle instructions into the instruction channel; the existing packet content and redaction stay unchanged
impact_assessment.risks: contract: packet format changes, existing tests and consumers read it as text; dependency: stdlib secrets only; concurrency: packet generation is local and per-run; state: none beyond the packet file
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests for matching fence ids, random ids per packet, a hostile commit subject inside the fence, and credential redaction; keep the prompt prefix outside the fence and the diff verbatim inside

[1/3] Add a fail-to-pass proof gate: run declared tests against the base tree, require an assertion failure there and a pass on the current tree

impact_assessment.why: IDEA-956 is the remaining approved AIKit idea: PRINCIPLE-014 requires a failing-first test, but no mechanical gate proves that a new test actually failed before the change
impact_assessment.benefits: A vacuous, already-passing or import-error test can no longer count as proof; the gate records base/current results and gives a deterministic exit code
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new CLI and JSON record; dependency: stdlib plus git; concurrency: a throwaway worktree per run; state: none written outside the temp tree
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure classifier unit tests plus an end-to-end temp-repo integration test; bounded subprocess timeouts; remove the worktree in finally; keep mutation scoring out of this milestone

[1/2] Add a Reforge analyzer adapter and analyze command that runs a reviewer command on a stage packet and records its findings

impact_assessment.why: Reforge only writes review packets; an empty reviewed_hunks list can pass a stage without any code analysis, so the tool does not do its core job.
impact_assessment.benefits: One command runs a real analyzer over the packet, validates its JSON through the existing review gate, and records findings; the analyzer is a pluggable command so any model or static tool can be used.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new analyze subcommand and reviewer command contract; dependency: stdlib subprocess/shlex only; concurrency: analyzer runs outside the state lock, review writes inside it; state: temp findings file plus existing reforge.json/ledger writes
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests with a fake analyzer and failure/timeout cases; no shell; timeout; typed errors; packet is already fenced as untrusted data; run Phase 4 gates
